requirements.title: Specification expressions default to constant expressions outside listed specification contexts
requirements.definition: A specification expression is an expression limited for specifications such as length type parameters and array bounds. A specification-expr shall be a constant expression unless it appears in an interface body, the specification part of a subprogram or BLOCK construct, a derived type definition, or the declaration-type-spec of a FUNCTION statement.

requirements.title: Specification expressions are restricted expressions
requirements.definition: The scalar-int-expr of a specification-expr shall be a restricted expression. A restricted expression permits only intrinsic operations or operations defined by specification functions, and only the listed primary forms; every subscript, section subscript, substring bound, and type parameter value in it is itself a restricted expression.

When such a function appears where a restricted expression requires a specification function, C1011 is the owning restriction.

requirements.title: Same specification-part dependencies used by specification inquiries are specified previously
requirements.definition: When a specification expression includes a specification inquiry depending on the type, a type parameter, an array bound, or a cobound of an entity specified in the same specification-part, that property is specified in a prior specification of the specification-part. The prior specification may appear to the left in the same statement but not within the same entity-decl. A reference to the value of an array element specified in the same specification-part requires the array to be completely specified in prior declarations.
